WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Bilateral trade relations with Israel 
 *401. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
 (a) the details of the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with Israel that 
was discussed earlier this year; 
 (b) whether there are any benefits to India with this agreement; 
 (c) if so, the details thereof; and 
 (d) whether bilateral trade relations between India and Israel 
have increased  
thereafter? 
 THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI ANAND SHARMA):  (a) The 
First Round of India — Israel Negotiations was held on 26th May, 2010 
in New Delhi. During these negotiations, a decision was taken that 
once the core issues are understood and parameters are  

 2 
outlined, then experts can be drawn for sectoral access . Both the 
sides agreed to exchange factual information, textual concepts. The 
second round of negotiations are slated for February, 2011 in 
Jerusalem (Israel). 
 (b) and (c) Yes, Sir. With the Free Trade Agreement, India stands 
to gain:— 
 • increase in export opportunities in rice, oilseeds, walnuts, 
meat, sugar, organic chemicals, polythene products, yarn, 
ladies garments, construction material, cement clinkers, iron 
and steel products, other metals products (copper especially), 
other vehicles (tractors), auto-components, textiles etc. 
 • There are Trade Barriers in Export of Agricultural Products 
and Meat Products to Israel. FTA will be beneficial for Indian 
Exporters to enhance their trade in these products. 
 • India’s strength lies in services sector whe reas Israel is 
strong in consultancy, engineering, Information Technology and 
Architecture. Both the countries stand to gain with this 
agreement. 
 (d) The negotiations are at a preliminary stage. It is too early 
to assess the impact of  
Free Trade Agreement after the first round of negotiations on 
bilateral trade relations  
between India and Israel. However, bilateral trade has registered an 
increase from US$ 1.1 billion to US$ 1.7 billion in April -July, 2010 
when compared to the corresponding period of the previous year. 
Migration from Leh-Ladakh villages adjoining Pakistan and China 
 †*402. SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether Government is aware that people of many villages of 
Leh, like Nobara, Turt uk, Partapur, Thang, Tuksi etc., adjoining the 
border with Pakistan and China are migrating in large scale because of 
lack of basic facilities, education and employment turning the area 
devoid of human habitation; and 
 (b) the measures including special schemes/programmes for 
development, being taken by Government for development and security of 
areas of Leh -Ladakh adjoining Pakistan border and villages adjoining 

 3 
China border? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) No, Sir. As per the report of the 
State Government, it is not a fact that people living in the areas 
adjoining the border of India with Pakistan and China are migrating 
because of lack of basic facilities. The State Government has  
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 4 
stated that various basic facilities have been provided to these 
areas. There are 231 educational and 99 medical institutions as well 
as 100% supply of safe drinking water under Rural Water Supply Scheme 
in the four border blocks, namely, Khaltse, Nobara, Durbuk and Nyoma. 
 (b) In addition, the Government of India’s Border Area Development 
Programme (BADP) which is under implementation in Jammu and Kashmir 
also provides coverage to the four border blocks concerne d in Leh -
Ladakh area. 100% non -lapsable Special Central Assistance is provided 
under this programme for execution of projects relating to 
infrastructure, livelihood, education, health, agriculture and allied 
sectors to meet the special developmental needs and inculcate a sense 
of security and well being among the people. The Government of India 
has allocated an average of Rs. 100 crore since 2002- 03 under this 
scheme to the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir. 
 The Ministry of Defence through the Army and the Ministry of Home 
Affairs through the Indo -Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) have also 
undertaken several measures under civic action programmes in education 
and information technology, infrastructure, healthcare, human resource 
development etc. for socio -economic development in Jammu and Kashmir 
including the Leh-Ladakh area. 
 A major initiative for development of the area is covered under 
Prime Minister’s Reconstruction Plan (PMRP) which has an allocation of 
Rs. 1200 crore for the current financial year. This involves 
development of broad based infrastructure and facilities in the field 
of power, environment and forests, tourism, agriculture and 
cooperation, food processing, roads etc.

Modernisation of CPMFs 
 *404. SHRI NARENDRA KUMAR KASHYAP: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether the Central Para-Military Forces (CPMFs) are not being 
provided with modern weapons and communication and other equipments; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof and action taken by Government in 
this regard; and 
 (c) the total funds allocated, released and utilized for 
modernisation of CPMFs during each of the last three years and till 
date, force-wise? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) No, Sir. The Government 

 7 
had approved a Five Year Plan (2002-07) for modernisation of 6 Central 
Para Military Forces — Assam Rifles (AR), Central Reserve Police Force 
(CRPF), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Border Security 
Force (BSF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), and National Security 
Guard (NSG) — at an estimated cost of Rs. 3740.71 crores in February, 
2002. The Government had also approved a Three Year Plan (2005-08) for 
modernization of Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) separately at an estimated 
cost of Rs. 444.43 crores in April 2005. Since the modernisation could 
not be completed according to the plan by 2007-08, the Government 

 8

objective of the Modernisation Plan is to equip the CPMFs for better 
strike capability, better mobility and to provide them state- of-the-
art communication, surveillance and protective systems. Details of 
items purchased under the Modernisation Plan by the CPMFs cannot be 
divulged for security reasons.

Programmes and training undertaken by NDMA 
 *405. SHRIMATI GUNDU SUDHARANI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
 (a) the programmes, trainings, etc. undertaken by the National 
Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) during the last three years, 
year-wise and State-wise; 
 (b) whether it is a fact that National Cyclone Risk Mitigation 
Project has been undertaken with the help of World Bank for Andhra 
Pradesh; 
 (c) if so, the details of programmes undertaken under the above 
Project in Andhra Pradesh; and 
 (d) the details of training given to Disaster Response Force to 

 9 
deal with cyclone, floods, etc., in Andhra Pradesh? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) The National Disaster Management 
Authority  

 10 
(NDMA), inter-alia, undertakes programmes on community awareness and 
training for capacity building. These include Training of Trainers 
(ToTs) for disaster management, training in search and rescue, mock 
exercises, awareness and disaster risk reduction programmes, as per 
details given in Statement- I, II, III, IV and V respectively ( See 
below). 
 (b) A National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) is proposed 
to be implemented in all the 13 cyclone prone coastal States and Union 
Territories including Andhra Pradesh. The proposed NCRMP will be 
implemented in three phases keeping in view the vulnerability of the 
States and their readiness with investment proposals. In Phase -I, it 
is proposed to cover Orissa and Andhra Pradesh. The World Bank has 
agreed to finance Phase -I of the NCRMP. The Project has not yet been 
launched and is presently being finalised for seeking approval of the 
competent authority. 
 (c) Activities proposed to be taken up in Andhra Pradesh under the 
project are construction of multipurpose cyclone shelters (including 
approach roads/bridges to  
habitations) and construction and renovation of embankments. The broad 
objectives of the projects are to upgrade cyclone forec asting, 
tracking and warning systems, cyclone risk mitigation and capacity 
building in multi-hazard risk management. Details in respect of major 
infrastructure works proposed to be taken up in Andhra Pradesh under

Statement-V 
Disaster Risk Reduction Programme 
 The National Disaster Management Authority is implementing GoI-UNDP 
Disaster Risk Reduction Programme (2009-12) with the overall objective 
of Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building for Disaster Risk 
Reduction. This project aims at strengthening the capacity building of 
disaster management institutions at the State and District levels. 
This project is being implemented in all the States and Delhi with 
their active participation. Annual Work Plan of 26 States including 
Delhi have been approved for an amount of Rs. 15.67 crores for 
implementation of the project during 2010-11. 
2. In addition, an amount of Rs. 0.59 crore has been approved to be 
released to National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) for 
development of Training Modules, Manuals and Guidelines for 
Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building for Disaster Risk 
Reduction (DRR).

to state: 
 (a) whether part of the payment reflected in documents and

 (b) whether it has been ensured that the other party would not 
increase the stipulated amount while delivering the carrier to India 
is 2012, as happened in case of 2004 agreement;  
and 
 (c) the truth behind the questions cropped up in the wake of 
forged payment of escalated costs? 
 THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI A.K. ANTONY): (a) No, Sir.

 (c) Does not arise. 
Compulsory registration of birth, death and marriage 

 22 
 †*407. MISS ANUSUIYA UI KEY: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to  
state: 
 (a) whether registration of birth, death and marriage has been 
made compulsory by Government; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 23 
 (b)    if so, details of the agency which carries out this work at 
State, district, development block and village level; 
 (c) the national average for registration of birth, death and 
marriage and whether the said registrations are being carried out as 
per the estimates of national average; and 
 (d) if not, the reasons therefor and the measures being taken by 
Government to ensure that these registrations are brought to national 
average? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY MAKEN): (a) The registration of births and dea ths in India 
is compulsory under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. 
The registration of marriages is not done under this Act. 
 (b) The Registration of births and deaths at State, District, 
Development Block and Village level is done by various agencies as 
detailed below:— 
 (i) State Level — This work is done by the Chief Registrar of 
Births and Deaths/Additional Chief Registrar of Births and 
Deaths. It is done in 17 States and 3 UTs by Health 
Department, in 10 States and 2 UTs by Economics, Statistics 
and Planning Department, in 1 State by Panchayat, in 1 UT by 
Revenue Department and in 1 UT by Local Administration 
Department. 
 (ii) District Level — The work is done by the District Registrar of 
Births and Deaths. For that, in 9 States/1 UT, Dis trict 
Magistrate/District Collectors, in 11 States/3 UTs Chief 
Medical Officer or equivalent, in 3 States/1 UT Deputy 
Commissioner/Survey and Settlement Officer, in 4 States/1 UT 
District Statistical Officer/District Planning Officer, in 1 
State Deputy Director of Panchayat and in 1 UT Deputy Director 
Local Administration Department have been authorized. 
 (iii) Development Block Level —  In most of the States/UTs, 
Block Development Officers (BDOs) have been authorized for 
this work. 
 (iv) Village Level — In 15 States/3 UTs officials of Panchayat 
Department, in 7 States/3 UTs Medical Officer or equivalent of 
Health Department, in 2 States School Teachers, in 3 States 
Officers/Officials of Revenue Department and in 1 State/1 UT 
Officer of Police Department have been authorized. 

 24 
 (c) Cent per cent registration of births and deaths is the 
national target but the same has not been achieved. At National level, 
about 74% births and 69% deaths are registered. The level of 
registration of birth and death varies from State to State. 
 (d) The main reasons for not achieving the target of cent per cent 
registration of birth and death are as follows:— 
 • Lack of awareness in general public about the necessity, 
importance and benefit of birth and death registration. 

 25 
 • Lack of utility of Birth and Death Certificate due to validity 
of other alternative documents. 
 • Lack of coordination between various departments engaged in 
registration  
work. 
 • Inadequate allocation of funds by States for this work. 
 Government of India is making efforts for achieving the target of 
cent per cent registration of birth and death. Continuous efforts are 
being made at national and State level to create awareness among the 
public about importance of registration of birth and death by means of 
various modes of publicity. Financial assistance for this purpose is 
also provided to the State Governments.

 53 
 (c) if so, the reasons therefor and the steps taken by Ministry to 
make Indian coffee competitive in the international market? 
 THE MINISTER OF STAT E IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA MADHAVRAO SCINDIA): (a) The production of coffee in 
Vietnam and Philippines in comparison to India is furnished 
hereunder:— 

 54 
 Year        India   Vietnam  
 Philippines 
  A B C A B C A B C 
2008-09 3.94 2.62 748 5.30 11.10 2090 1.23 0.17 138 
2009-10 3.99 2.90 826 5.30 10.80 2030 1.23 0.18 146 
A – Area in lakh ha. B – Production in lakh MTC – Productivity in

 The production of coffee in Vietnam is higher while in Philippines 
it is much less in comparison to India. Robusta is being predominantly 
cultivated in Vietnam and the total area under coffee is 5.30 lakh ha. 
with a production of 11 lakh MT at the productivity level of 2000 
kg./ha. Coffee in Vietnam is being cultivated in more ideal conditions 
like open condition, well distributed rainfall with 2 to 3 months of 
dry period, deep fertile volcanic soils, copious irrigation facilities 
coupled with large scale use of fertilizers etc. In India, the total 
area under coffee is 3.99 lakh ha. with a production of 2.90 lakh MT 
at a productivity level of 800 kg./ha. The agro -climatic conditions 
prevailing in coffee zones of the country are not ideal for achieving 
high productivity as in the case of Vietnam. High temperatures in 
summer coupled with 3 months of heavy rainfall during monsoon followed 
by 4- 6 months of dry conditions impose limitations for coffee 
productivity. However, in order to mitigate these factors, coffee is 
grown under shade tree canopy and despite this; India is placed at 6th 
position as the producing country in the world. Further, there are no 
new areas suitable for coffee expansion in Traditional areas of 
Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu except in Non- Traditional areas of 
Andhra Pradesh and Orissa and North East Region where coffe e 
cultivation is encouraged for social upliftment of local tribals and 
prevent Jhum cultivation. 
 (b) and (c) No, Sir. Quality of Indian coffee is not inferior. 
Rather, we have been fetching premium prices in the international 
market due to its quality standards.

Central Government that essential commodities like rice, pulses,

this regard? 

 60 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY  
(SHRI JYOTIRADITYA MADHAVRAO SCINDIA): (a) and (b) In the month of 
March, 2007, a request was received from the Chief Minister, Tamil 
Nadu, to suspend the on -line trading in all essential commodities as 
an interim measure, so that their prices could be kept in check. An 
Expert Committee was set up by the Government under the Chairmanship 
of Prof. Abhijit Sen, Member, Planning Commission to study the extent 
of impact, if any, of the futures trading on the wholesale and retail 
prices of agricultural commodities. In its report submitted in April, 
2008, the Committee was unable to determine any conclusive casual 
relationship in view of short time period during which futures markets 
have functioned and complexities arising out of the fact that a large 
number of variables impact the spot prices. The trends since 2007 also 
showed that in commodities where futures trading was suspended or 
there is no futur e trading like urad and tur and fruits and

where futures trading exists e.g. chana. Accordingly, the Government 
does not favour a ban on the futures trading.

National Disaster Management guidelines on Tsunamis 
 3181. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to  
state: 
 (a) what are the National Disaster Management Guidelines on 
Tsunamis as released by Government; 
 (b) by when the guidelines would come into effect for coastal 
States and details thereof; 
 (c) the financial support and technical expertise to be provided 
by Government to State Governments such as Tamil Nadu to implement the 
above-mentioned guidelines; 
 (d) whether the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System is currently 
functioning and if so, its salient features and details thereof; and 
 (e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 THE MINISTER  OF STATE I N THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI 
MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) The National Disaster 
Management Guidelines on Management of Tsunami has been released 
during August, 2010 by the National Disaster Management Authority 
(NDMA) under Section 6(2)(d) of the Disaster Management Act, 2005. It 
covers various aspects of the Tsunami preparedness, Tsunami early 
warning system, Tsunami mitigation and emergency response. The 
guidelines issued by NDMA becomes effective from the date of 

 208 
issue/release. 
 (c) The National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) has been 
providing financial and technical support to the Disaster Management 
Centres of the Administrative Training Institutes of the States 
including that in Tamil Nadu for training and capacity building of the 
government functionaries on various aspects of disaster management 
including management of Tsunami disaster. 
 †Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 

 209 
 (d) The Indian Tsunami Early Warning System has been established in 
collaboration with the Department of Space (DOS), Department of 
Science and Technology (DST) and the Council of Scientific and 
Industrial Research (CSIR). It comprises a real -time network of 
seismic stations, Bottom Pressure Recorders (BPPRs) and tike gauges to 
detect tsunamigenic earthquakes and to monitor tsunamis and to provide 
timely advisories to vulnerable community by means of latest 
communication methods with back- end support of scenario database, 
vulnerability modeling and Decision Support System. Th e seismic 
subsystem receives real -time seismic data from the national seismic 
network of the Indian Meteorogical Department (IMD) and other 
International seismic networks and is capable of detecting all 
earthquake events occurring in the Indian Ocean in le ss than 10 
minutes of occurrence. BPRs installed in the deep ocean are the key 
sensors to confirm the triggering of a tsunami over the Bay of Bengal 
and the Arabian Sea. Thirty coastal tidal stations have been Installed 
by the Survey of India (SOI) to monitor the progress of tsunami waves. 
Tsunami N2 model has been customized by Integrated Coastal and Marine 
Area Management (ICMAM) and Indian National Centre for Ocean 
Information Services (INCOIS) for the purpose of predicting surges for 
different scenarios  of earthquakes and to indicate the extent of 
Inundation of seawater Into the land. This information has been used 
for taking precautionary and mitigation measures such as evacuation of 
people, Avoiding human settlements, large investment, designing of 
appropriate structures, etc. in the risk prone areas. 
 (e) In view of reply to (d), does not arise.

 3188. SHRI AVTAR SINGH KARIMPURI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state:

the State of Jammu and Kashmir till date;

rehabilitation of  
persons;

Loss due to cyclone Laila in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh 
 †3190. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to  
state: 
 (a) whether it is a fact that recently there has been heavy loss 
of life and property in the coastal areas of Tamil Nadu and Andhra 
Pradesh due to cyclone ‘Laila’; 
 (b) if so, the details thereof; 
 (c) in a situation when frequency of natural disasters is 
increasing due to climate  
change, whether special arrangements are being made by Government to 
deal with such disaster; and 
 (d) if so, the details thereof? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE I N THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI 
MULLAPPALLY RAMACHANDRAN): (a) and (b) As per information received 
from India Meteorological Department, a severe cyclonic storm 
developed over Bay of Bengal and crossed Andhra Pradesh coast near 
Bapatla on 20th May, 2 010 evening between 1630 and 1730 hrs. IST.  

 236 
This disturbance inter-alia caused very heavy rainfall over north 
Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh. 
 According to the report from the State Government of Andhra 
Pradesh, 22 human lives were lost, 2075 cattle heads perished, 14298 
houses damaged and crops over an area of 26685 ha. were affected due 
to the cyclone. The Government of Tamil Nadu has reported that 11 
human lives were lost and 8 cattle heads perished due to this cyclone. 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
 (c) and (d) The Government of India has enacted a Disaster 
Management Act, 2005 for effective management of disasters. It inter-
alia, provides for strengthening institutional mechanisms at National, 
State and District levels for drawing up and monitoring the 
implementation of disaster management plans, ensuring measures by 
various wings of Government for preventing and mitigating the effects 
of disasters as well as for undertaking a holistic, coordinated and 
prompt response to any disaster situation. 
 The Government of India has also prepared the National policy on 
Disaster Management (NPDM) with a vision to build a safe and disaster 
resilient India by developing a holistic, proactive, multi -disaster 
oriented and technology driven strategy through a culture of 
prevention, mitigation, preparedness and response. The Policy covers 
all aspects of disaster management covering institutional, legal and 
financial arrangements; disaster prevention, mitigation and 
preparedness, techno -legal regi me; response, relief and 
rehabilitation; reconstruction and recovery; capacity development; 
knowledge management and research and development. 
 The National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM) envisages Hazard 
zonation, mapping and vulnerability analysis in a multi- hazard 
framework utilizing Geographic Information System (GIS) based 
databases such as National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) 
and National Spatial Data Infrastructure (NSDI). The NPDC also 
stresses the need to establish, upgrade and m odernize the forecasting 
and early warning systems for all types of disasters. 
 Such measures are expected to strengthen and enhance the functional 
capability for response, relief and rehabilitation and reduce the 
adverse impact of natural disasters, inclu ding climate change, in the 
country.

Social security benefits for labour 
 3204. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA KHUNTI A: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether Government is aware that 85 per cent of the employed 
labour force has no access to social security benefits; 
 (b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
 (c) the fresh steps taken by Government to bring entire labour 
force under social security benefits network such as provident fund, 
gratuity, health care, pension etc.? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT  
(SHRI HARISH RAWAT): (a) to (c) As per survey carr ied out by the 
National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) in 2004 -05, the total 
employment in both Organised and Unorganised sector in the country was 
of the order of 45.9 crore. Out of this about 2.6 crore was in the 
Organised Sector and the balance 43.3 crore in the Unorganised Sector. 
 With regard to Social Security to the organised sector workers, it 
is being extended to workers as per provisions of various Acts such 
as:— 
 (i) Employees State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948, 

 258 
 (ii) Employees’ Provident Fund an d Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 
1952, 
 (iii) The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, 

 259 
 (iv) Maternity Benefit (MB) Act, 1961 and 
 (v) Workmen’s (now Employees’) Compensation (WC) Act, 1923. 
 With regard to social security to unorganized workers, the 
Government enacted the Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008. 
The Act provides for constitution of National Social Security Board 
which shall recommend social security schemes viz. life and disability 
cover, health maternity benefits, old age protection and any other 
benefit as may be determined by the Government for unorganized 
workers. 
 The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) providing for smart card 
based cashless health insurance cover of Us. 30000 to BPL families (a 
unit of five) In the unorganized sector was launched on 01.10.2007 and 
became operational from 01.04.2008. More than 2.18 crore BPL families 
(a unit of five) have been covered under RSBY as on 30.11.2010. 
 The scheme has been extended to building and other construction 
workers registered und er the Building and other Construction Workers 
(Regulation of Employment of Condition of Service), Act, 1996 and 
street vendors. 
 In the Budget for the year 2010-11, the Government has announced to 
extend benefits of RSBY to all such MGNREGA beneficiaries who have 
worked for more than 15 days during the preceding financial year. 
Steps are being taken to extend RSBY to MGNREGA beneficiaries. 
 To provide death and disability cover to rural landless households 
between the age group of the 18 to 59 years, the G overnment launched 
the “Aam Admi Bima Yojana ”. More than 1.45 crore persons have been 
covered under the scheme as on 31.07.2010. 
 Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension has been expanded by 
revising the criteria of eligibility. All citizens above the age of 65 
years and living below poverty line are eligible for benefits under 
the scheme. The Government also launched the National Pension Scheme 
called Swavalamban Scheme for unorganized sector workers. 
 The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 was e nacted 
providing for the enhancement of livelihood security of the households 
in rural areas of the country by providing  
at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial 
year to every  
household. 

 260 
 In addition to above, the Government is implementing various social 
security schemes viz. Swarnjayanti Gram Swarojgar Yojana, Swarnjayanti 
Shahari Rojgar Yojana, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation 
Programme, National Social Assistance Programme, etc. providing for 
social security to the workers in the unorganized sector. 
 The Government have set up Welfare Funds to provide social 
security/welfare measures to certain categories of workers i.e. beedi 
workers, certain non -coal mine workers and cine workers, the welfare 
measures include health ca re, housing, educational assistance for 
children, drinking water supply, etc.

Collaboration with IRF to reduce road fatalities 
 3229. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
 (a) whether according to International Road Federation (IRF) a 
global body for promoting and advocating safe road developments, India 
accounts for 10 per cent of the 13 lakh road accident deaths world 
wide every year; 
 (b) if so, what i nitiatives Government has so far taken in 
collaboration with IRF to reduce rate of road fatalities in country; 
 (c) whether Government proposes to consider road safety measures 
either  
through any changes in the Motor Vehicles Act or through engineering 
measures;  
and 
 (d) the details of findings/outcome of discussion of two day 
global meet of 20 countries held in Delhi recently? 
 THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI MAHADEV S. KHANDELA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in collaboration with 
International Road Federation (IRF) has already undertaken a number of 
measures such as:— 
 (i) The State Governments have been requested to extend support to 
IRF in promoting road safety campaign, di splay of hoardings, 
featuring of promotional films on road safety in Cinema halls 
as also on television, and seeking support of the print media 
to carry forward the road safety campaigns. 
 (ii) A circular has been issued on 27th April, 2010 to all 
concerned to implement the desired engineering measures both 
on existing roads as well as in ongoing Road projects 

 301 
 (iii) The Ministry has taken up the matter with the Ministry of 
Human Resource Development regarding incorporation of a 
separate chapter on Road saf ety in the school curriculum and 
to print the road signs with their meanings in front and back 
inside cover of all school text book for mass awareness 
 (iv) The Ministry has also taken up with the Ministry of Finance to 
provide tax exemption to the donors of the corporate world and 
philanthropist individual who extend a helping hand by 
incurring expenditure towards Road Safety programmes. 

 302 
 (c) The task of arresting road accidents involves a multi -pronged 
approach. The main thrust of accident prevention and control across 
the world has been on 4 E’s, vis. (i) Education, (ii) Enforcement, 
(iii) Engineering and (iv) Environment and Emergency care of road 
accident victims. The Government of India is focusing on all these 4 
approaches in its policies and programmes on road safety issues. 
 (d) An International seminar on road accidents and safety was held 
by International Road Federation (IRF) —  India Chapter in New Delhi 
during 25th- 26th November, 2010. Important decisions taken in the 
seminar are as follows:— 
 (i) To earmark a non lapsable grant of Rs.  5,000 crore every year 
as Road Safety Fund, which shall be administered by Road 
Safety Board. 
 (ii) To establish an autonomous Road Safety Board at the Centre and 
similar Boards at State level in the next one year. Funding of 
these Boards could be provided from Central Road Fund and from 
the Plan Funds. 
 (iii) To earmark 10% of the project cost for road safety features. 
 (iv) To issue circulars to all the automobile manufactures to 
provide all modern in-vehicle safety devices. 
 (v) To establish Fast Track Courts, using the services of retired 
Judges, to deal with insurance claims of the road accident 
victims and traffic violation cases. 
 (vi) All hospitals to provide immediate medical care to accident 
victims. 
 (vii) A robust accident data recording and management system be 
developed. 
 (viii) Road Safety Audit Report and its compliance, in respect of 
project design, be made mandatory for according administrative 
approval of estimates. 
 (ix) To develop Road Safety curriculum in the school syllabus.

below). 
 (b) Depending upon the counts of the yarn, increase in the yarn 
prices are in the range of 34% to 43% from January, 2009 to August, 
2010. The basic reason for increase in the prices of cotton yarn is 
increasing price of cotton. 
 (c) The Group of Ministers met on 14th and 28th September, 2010 to 
discuss the issue of cotton security in the backdrop of steep increase 
in the cotton. In the meeting, the decisions taken, int er alia , 
include (i) registration of cotton export contract would commence from 
1.10.2010 instead of 15.9.2010; (ii) actual exports would commence 
from 1.11.2010; and (iii) the exportable surplus was identified as 55 
lakh bales. 
 With a view to increase th e availability of cotton yarn at 
reasonable price to domestic industry, including handloom initiatives 
have been taken such as (i) Hank Yarn Obligation expanded from 40s 
counts to 80s counts w.e.f. 31.03.2010; (ii) Strict monitoring of hank 
yarn obligation started from 01.04.2010; (iii) registration of cotton 
yarn export with Office of Textile Commissioner was made mandatory 
w.e.f. 09.04.2010. 
 The Government has constituted Cotton Yarn Advisory Board (CYAB) on 
13th September, 2010 to monitor the domestic a nd international prices 
of cotton yarn and suggest measures for increasing the availability of 
cotton yarn at reasonable prices for domestic consumption. It has also 
been decided that there shall be no further registration of cotton 
yarn exports beyond 720 million kg. during 2010-11.
